cohort: The study included women with subfertility (n=3188 singleton, n=350 twin) and unexposed women (n=52443 singleton, n=1125 twin) delivering at Aberdeen Maternity Hospital between 1992 and 2009.
finding: Subfertility per se, rather than fertility treatment, was associated with an increased risk of adverse outcomes in singleton pregnancies, including pre-eclampsia, antepartum haemorrhage, induction of labour, and very preterm delivery.
mod_finding: Subfertile women delivering twins were at a higher risk of being delivered by emergency caesarean section.
